questions.prompt: An expert has the bash tool and a gate that blocks rm -rf. The model runs cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519. Why can it work?
options: bash runs as a different, more powerful user
The working folder only sets the start path and does not stop access to other paths
The gate blocks only commands that the model writes in capital letters
pi disables all gates when bash is on
questions.explanation: The working folder does not prevent commands from reaching other paths available to the pi process. No gate named that file, so nothing stopped the command.

questions.prompt: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is set when you start pi. What does a bash command receive?
options: No environment variables, unless you list them
Only variables that start with PI_
Every variable of the pi process, including the key
questions.explanation: getShellEnv() returns the whole process environment plus PATH, and bash passes it to the child shell.

questions.prompt: Why is the SQL expert, with read, sql_schema and sql_query, safer than an expert with bash?
options: It has no tool that starts a shell, so it cannot run arbitrary commands
It runs in a container by default
pi gives it a smaller environment
questions.explanation: Without bash there is no tool that starts a shell with the account's rights, so a command like cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 has no way to run.
